info.title: warte agent API
info.description: Machine-readable answers for agents, from the ground station's latest snapshot. Read-only. Start estimates, history and reports are under /api (/api/eta, /api/status.md, /api/report, /api/history/fleet).

get.summary: Fleet queue: self-hosted runners, hosted pool, and optionally one repo

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name without the org, e.g. spar

400.description: repo is not a bare repository name

503.description: no ground station configured, or no snapshot received yet

get.summary: Should an agent open a PR of this kind in this repo now?
get.description: security and red-main are always open. docs batch whenever the repo has CI in flight. fix and feature use thresholds kept in warte. Stale data (snapshot older than 5 minutes) never gates: the verdict is open and the reason says so.

400.description: missing or invalid repo or kind

503.description: no ground station configured, or no snapshot received yet

get.summary: When will the next job of a PR (or branch) start?
get.description: Estimated from MEASURED waits (started_at - created_at of jobs that started in the same pool over the last 3h), not from queue position: GitHub does not start jobs in creation order. Covers the next job only; jobs gated by needs: are not created yet. status=unknown means the org scan was truncated or a telemetry chunk was lost, so absence does not prove the PR is not queued.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository name without the org, e.g. spar

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Head branch (for push runs); used when pr is absent

503.description: no ground station configured, or no snapshot received yet

get.summary: Trend points, one per minute
Fleet status as Markdown (for terminals and agents)

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: With pr or branch: answer the ETA question as Markdown instead

get.summary: The same report as JSON

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: YYYY-MM; default the current UTC month

get.summary: Monthly conveyor-belt report as Markdown
get.description: Work (completed-started) vs wait (started-created) per pool and workflow from every finished job, flow efficiency, per-runner utilisation, hosted peak concurrency, and by hour of day whether waiting was scheduling (eligible runners were free) or capacity (they were busy). Only COMPLETE days (closed and matching the agent's manifest) are analysed; without any, the report is marked preliminary and the bottleneck verdict is withheld.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: YYYY-MM; default the current UTC month

get.summary: Long-poll: hold until a PR's or branch's CI runs start or finish
get.description: Answers at once when the CI state differs from the cursor in since; otherwise holds until a snapshot changes it or timeout passes (changed: false). Without since, the state at the call is the baseline. Pass the returned cursor as since on the next call so no change is missed. Resolution is one snapshot (about a minute). At most 8 held requests per client and 1024 in total. The CLI is warte watch --ci.

parameters.name: pr
parameters.description: PR number; give exactly one of pr or branch

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Seconds to hold, default 300, at most 900

200.description: Changed, or held until the timeout

400.description: missing or invalid repo, pr/branch, since or timeout

503.description: no ground station, no snapshot yet, or too many watchers

get.summary: Is this host low on disk, and how much do agents hold there?
get.description: A verdict per writable volume from the host's latest probe report; the host's verdict is its worst volume. Thresholds are warte's config ([pressure] low_gb, default 20; critical_gb, default 10). Per volume, the GB agent scratchpads, target/ directories and worktrees hold, as totals only: no session, repo, pid or path (who holds it: `warte probe pressure` on that machine). unknown when there is no fresh report.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: The host as its probe enrolled (`warte probe pressure` prints it)

400.description: host missing; the body lists the known hosts

404.description: no report from that host; the body lists the known hosts

get.summary: What is forecast to reach its limit?
get.description: Per reporting machine, a straight line through the last week's hourly means of each disk's used share and of memory use. A forecast is listed when the line rises steadily (R² at least 0.7), rests on at least 24 hours and 12 points, and reaches 95% within 14 days at its current rate; each carries its evidence. Series with too little data are counted, never forecast. Within 3 days a forecast is an amber outage finding, within 1 day a red one.

503.description: no ground station with history configured

get.summary: Do the names CI depends on resolve, and through which resolvers?
get.description: The latest round of the [canaries] DNS checks: every configured name through every resolver (by label, never by address), each with its outcome and how many rounds in a row it has failed, plus findings naming the likely cause of failures two rounds old: a resolver, the dependency's DNS, or warte's network.

200.description: the latest round and its findings

503.description: no canaries configured, or the first round has not finished

get.summary: What runs out, and when?
get.description: warte's own certificates, every certificate the [expiry] endpoints send and the [expiry] PEM files hold (by label and place in the chain), the [expiry] dates, and the token each job last used, soonest first, plus findings for end dates within amber_days (amber) or red_days (red). Addresses and paths are never shown.

200.description: everything that runs out, and its findings

get.summary: Is CI getting worse? This week against the week before
get.description: From the finished-job ledger: per repository and overall, finished jobs, failures and flaky jobs (failed, then passed on a re-run) for each week; per runner pool the 90th-percentile queue wait; the median release run; and warnings for large changes resting on enough data. Recomputed at most every 10 minutes.

200.description: the two weeks and the warnings

get.summary: Every machine the ground station hears from, with drift findings
get.description: Latest probe report per machine (OS, kernel, CPU, memory, disks, agent CLIs and their versions, agent sessions without command lines), its age and a stale flag (no report for 3 minutes), plus findings: kernel or tool versions behind the newest seen, full disks, low memory, overload, silence.

get.summary: The latest notional-cost report of agent chats and subagents
get.description: Notional list price, not billed. Per session, per subagent (last 90 days) and rollups per day, month and the last 30 days by repository, model and task category, plus the share of subagent work on a cheaper tier than its caller. report is null until a workstation has pushed one.

200.description: the stored report with its age, or report null

post.summary: Replace the notional-cost report (a workstation job, nightly)
post.description: The body is the whole report (schema 1 or 2, kind claude-code-costs; `warte docs costs-schema`). Schema 2 adds weekly counts: advisor calls, compactions, cross-session messages, SendMessage calls, and per repository and skill tool uses, tool errors, permission denials, failure streaks and loop-guard firings. Unknown fields, free text and negative or non-finite amounts are rejected. At most 8 MiB.

400.description: not a valid report; nothing stored

get.summary: The latest briefing, or the one of ?from=YYYY-MM-DD, with the periods kept
get.description: Every two days: one plain line, three bullets, and the facts they were made from (public repositories only: merged pull requests, closed issues, releases, pull requests open for more than a day, CI runs and failed jobs, a notional token check, setup changes). source is template or model.

200.description: briefing (null before the first period closes) and periods, newest first

post.summary: A model run's text for a period (needs briefing:write)
post.description: Body: from, model, line, bullets (exactly 3). Kept only when every repository, #number, version and count it names is in that period's facts and the text has at most 130 words, no links and no markup; otherwise 422 with the reason, and the template stays.

422.description: the text does not fit the facts; the template stays

get.summary: The facts of the latest period, for the run that writes the text

200.description: from, until, source, facts and the rules a text must meet

get.summary: Issues people opened in the org's public repositories, waiting for a first reply
get.description: ready: the oldest queued issues the hour still allows (per_hour), each with repo, number, title (untrusted, cut to 120 characters), author, url and action; waiting: how many wait beyond that; recent: the last ones done. Bots, configured logins and issues whose body carries an agent marker are never queued.

post.summary: The reply run is done with an issue (needs triage:write)
post.description: Body: repo, number, outcome (replied, asked or skipped). warte never writes to GitHub; the run posts as its own bot.

422.description: not queued, or an unknown outcome

get.summary: Who this browser is signed in as
get.description: {auth: false} without [auth]; with it, {auth: true, user: null} or user {sub, name, role}. Login is through the OIDC provider (/auth/login); warte never sees a password.

get.summary: The latest skill-usage report of every source
get.description: Which agent skills were invoked (model, user slash command, subagent), in how many sessions, and which installed skills were never used, from local agent transcripts. reports is empty until a workstation has pushed one.

200.description: the stored reports with their ages

post.summary: Replace the skill-usage report of its source (a workstation job, nightly)
post.description: Needs the skills:write right. The body is the whole report (schema skill-usage.v1). Unknown fields, free text, a source other than [a-z0-9-]{1,32} and a name other than [a-z0-9._:-]{1,64} are rejected. At most 1 MiB.

400.description: not a valid report; nothing stored

get.summary: The fleet model (a spar instance of the Warte_Fleet AADL types) and its differences from what reports in

503.description: the configured model could not be read

get.summary: This document

not_enough_data.description: of those, series with too little data to forecast

checked_at.description: when endpoints and files were last checked; 0 before the first check

measured_at.description: When the report was taken (unix seconds)

held_measured_at.description: When the probe last sized what agents hold; null when it has not (it sizes only while a volume is low)

estimate.description: null when the pool has fewer than 5 recent samples

overdue.description: already waited longer than 90% of recent jobs: starved, stuck, or unservable labels

recheck_after_s.description: Seconds until asking again is worth it, for an agent's next wake-up: 300..1800, the soonest of running (900), queued with estimate (window start, or halfway to its end), queued without estimate (900), overdue (1800); unknown = 600. Absent for not_queued: act now.

queued_complete.description: False: the queue scan was incomplete, so a missing run may still be queued

recheck_s.description: Seconds until asking again is worthwhile; absent for open
